Unit 1 of 10: The Cartesian Plane

Key ideas

  • Two perpendicular number lines — the x-axis (horizontal) and y-axis (vertical) — meet at the origin O (0, 0).
  • Every point is named by an ordered pair (x, y): x = abscissa (distance along the x-axis), y = ordinate.
  • Order matters: (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points.
  • The system is named after René Descartes; coordinates let us describe locations exactly, like a floor plan on a grid.

Worked examples

Example 1: What are the coordinates of the origin, and of a point 3 units right of it on the x-axis? Answer: (0, 0) and (3, 0).

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The abscissa of (−4, 7) is: (a) 7 (b) −4 (c) 3 (d) 11. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) What is the ordinate of any point on the x-axis? Answer: 0.
  3. (2 marks) Are (3, 8) and (8, 3) the same point? Explain. Answer: no (1); the first number is x, the second is y — order matters (1).
  4. (3 marks) Write the coordinates of: (i) a point on the y-axis 5 units below O (ii) a point 2 units left of O on the x-axis (iii) the origin. Answer: (0, −5) (1); (−2, 0) (1); (0, 0) (1).
  5. (3 marks) In a classroom grid with the door at (0, 0), Asha sits 4 columns right and 3 rows forward; Ravi sits 1 column left and 2 rows forward. Write their coordinates and the horizontal gap between them. Answer: Asha (4, 3) (1); Ravi (−1, 2) (1); horizontal gap 4 − (−1) = 5 columns (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Writing (y, x). 2. Origin as (1, 1). 3. Ordinate on the x-axis non-zero. 4. Ignoring signs. 5. Confusing abscissa and ordinate.

Quick recall

  1. Horizontal axis? 2. Origin? 3. Abscissa means? 4. Ordinate means? 5. Named after?

Answers: 1) x-axis. 2) (0, 0). 3) x-coordinate. 4) y-coordinate. 5) Descartes.
